examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring Alternative Forms of the Secant-Tangent Identity
examples.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(3),$ as follows:

$$
\dfrac{\color{blue}1}{\sec{\theta}+\tan{\theta}} = \dfrac{\color{blue}\sec^2{\theta} - \tan^2{\theta}}{\sec{\theta} + \tan{\theta}}
$$

Next, we can further simplify our expression by factoring the numerator as a difference of squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta +\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta } & =\frac{(\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta -\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta )(\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta +\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta )}{\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta +\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta -\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta )\cancel{(\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta +\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta )}}{\cancel{(\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta +\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta )}} \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta -\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\dfrac{1}{\sec\theta + \tan\theta} =  \sec{\theta} - \tan{\theta}.
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\frac{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1}=\frac{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }
$$

Next, we recall the following identity: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }
$$

Using the above identity, we can further simplify our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{\cancel{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }} \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{1}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1}=\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta .
$$
